1.n: Odysseus, named at the end of the line
under the two bushes, in the bed of leaves where Book 5 left him (5.476–493)

2.n: dative of cause with ἀρημένος; with καμάτῳ perhaps one idea, 'the sleep that weariness brings' (Merry on 6.2)

2.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
2.n: a perfect participle with no other forms: 'afflicted, worn down', as Iliad 18.435; its derivation is uncertain; a few manuscripts read βεβαρημένος (Merry's critical note and note on 6.2)

3.n: the people of Scheria (8); Φαιήκων ἀνδρῶν again 114, 202
'land, country' with its people; second accent from enclitic τε

4.n: accent from enclitic ποτʼ; their former home, as against the move of 7–8
'with broad dancing floors' (εὐρύς + χορός), an epithet of towns, later merely 'spacious' (Merry on 6.4); two-termination adjective
the Phaeacians' former home, near the Cyclopes (5); known only from this passage; not the spring Hypereia of the Iliad (2.734, 6.457)

5.n: the race of Polyphemus (1.69–71), whose land Odysseus tells of in Book 9

5.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. pl. masc.
5.n: uncontracted; 'behaving arrogantly' (ὑπέρ + ἀνήρ), a participle whose present is not otherwise found; in the Odyssey usually of the suitors, in the Iliad of the Trojans (4.176) and of Deiphobus (13.258) (Merry on 6.5)

6.n: the Cyclopes; accented before enclitic σφεας
epic σφέας = αὐτούς, enclitic here, one syllable (synizesis): the Phaeacians
iter. (-σκ-), unaugmented: 'kept harming, robbing'; the iterative only here in Homer
epic -φι, here dative of respect: the reason they could oppress their neighbors (Merry on 6.6)

7.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
7.n: transitive aorist: 'made (them) rise up', i.e. removed them from their homes
unaugmented (= ἦγε), not the imperative; imperfect of the journey, the aorist εἷσεν (8) of the settling that completed it (Merry on 6.7)
son of Poseidon and Periboea, king of the Phaeacians and father of Alcinous (7.56–63); dead before the story (11)

8.n: causative aorist εἷσα 'made sit', i.e. settled
dative of place without a preposition, the reading of Aristarchus; others read δʼ ἐν Σχερίῃ, Apollonius ἐς Σχερίην (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.8)
epic gen. pl. -άων, in apposition to ἀνδρῶν; disputed, as at 1.349: 'gain-getting, toiling' (ἀλφάνω 'earn') or 'bread-eating' (ἄλφιτον + ἔδω)

9.n: adverbial, with the dative πόλει: 'round the city'; or in tmesis with ἔλασσε
walls come first, as the mark of a 'fenced city' after their experience of dangerous neighbors (Merry on 6.9)
unaugmented, epic -σσ- (= ἤλασε): 'drew' a wall round, as ἀμφὶ δὲ τάφρον ἤλασαν Iliad 7.449–450
aorist middle of δέμω 'build': 'built for himself (and his people)'

10.n: = ἐδάσσατο, epic -σσ-: 'allotted' the land for tilling (Merry on 6.10)
plowland; of a family's lands also Iliad 22.489 (Merry on 6.10)

11.n: κήρ 'doom', not κῆρ 'heart'; instrumental with δαμείς

11.p: verb · aor. part. pass. nom. sg. masc.

11.n: Ἄϊδος (gen. of Ἄϊς = Ἀΐδης: '(the house) of Hades') with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word, as 3.410

12.n: son of Nausithous (7.63), king of the Phaeacians and husband of Arete (7.54); first named here
accent thrown back (anastrophe): placed after its noun

12.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

14.n: epic dat. -ῆϊ; dative of interest: 'for Odysseus'

14.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
14.n: epic diectasis -όωσα (= μητιῶσα); the line again 8.9

15.n: unaugmented root aorist (= ἔβη); βῆ δʼ ἴμεν 'set out to go'
epic ἐνί = ἐν; after its noun, accent thrown back (anastrophe)

16.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι; used as a noun, 'the immortal goddesses'; dative with ὁμοίη
accusative of respect; φυὴν καὶ εἶδος as Iliad 22.370

17.n: daughter of Alcinous, named here for the first time, in apposition to κούρη (15)
epic gen. -οιο; θυγάτηρ μεγαλήτορος Ἀλκινόοιο again 196, 213

18.n: epic apocopated πάρ = παρά; adverbial, with κοιμῶντο understood from κοιμᾶτʼ (16)
they slept in their young mistress's room, close to the door (Merry on 6.18); two handmaids attend Penelope too (1.331)
genitive with ἄπο; Homer gives the Graces no number and names only one, Pasithea (Iliad 14.275–276) (Merry on 6.18)
accent thrown back (anastrophe): placed after its noun

18.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. fem.

19.n: epic gen./dat. dual -οιιν: one maid by each doorpost, so that the door could not be opened without waking them (Merry on 6.18); or genitive with ἑκάτερθε, 'on either side of'; the form only here in Homer
plural of the two leaves of the door
'lay to' on their doorposts, i.e. were shut (Merry on 6.19)

20.n: ἀνέμου ὡς πνοιή 'like a breath of wind'; Merry on 6.20 compares Hermes slipping through a keyhole 'like an autumn breeze' (Hymn to Hermes 146)
epic athematic aorist (ἐπεσσύμην), + acc. of the goal δέμνια

21.n: unaugmented root aorist (= ἔστη); the line = 4.803 (the phantom at Penelope's head), Iliad 23.68, 24.682: dream figures stand over the sleeper
in tmesis with ἔειπεν (προσεῖπον 'speak to'), with two accusatives, μιν and μῦθον
epic ἔειπε (= εἶπε); in tmesis with πρός

22.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.

22.n: epic gen. -οιο; 'famous for ships' (ναῦς + κλειτός), only here in Homer; the Phaeacians are ναυσίκλυτοι (7.39, 8.191)
a Phaeacian, known only from this line; not Hecuba's father Dymas (Iliad 16.718)

23.n: the daughter of Dymas; accented before enclitic οἱ
Nausicaa; dative with ὁμηλικίη and with κεχάριστο
abstract for concrete, = ὁμῆλιξ 'age-mate', as 3.49 (Merry on 6.23); predicate, + dat.
unaugmented pluperfect, passive in sense: 'she was dear', + dat.; the pluperfect only here in Homer

24.n: the daughter of Dymas; dative with ἐεισαμένη: 'likening herself to her' (Merry on 6.24)
object of προσέφη, not a reflexive with ἐεισαμένη (Merry on 6.24)

24.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.

25.n: enclitic, = νυν; accented before enclitic σʼ
'slack, negligent', as Iliad 2.241; predicative: 'Why hath thy mother such a lazy daughter in thee?', in contrast to the thrifty housewifery of the queen (Merry on 6.25)

26.n: answered by σοὶ δέ (27); accent from enclitic τοι
epic τοι = σοι; dative of interest
singular verb with neuter plural subject
a fixed epithet, which does not clash with ἀκηδέα (Merry on 6.26)

27.n: used as a noun: 'fine things'; answered by τὰ δέ (28), as if καλὰ δέ (Merry on 6.27)

28.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; antecedent of οἵ
epic = ἄν; with the subjunctive, of what is expected (Merry on 6.27)

middle 'lead home (as a bride)': the bridegroom's family, or rather the torchlit procession that brought the bride to her new home (Iliad 18.492–493), whose members the bride might dress in fine clothes (Merry on 6.28)

29.n: 'report, talk' (φημί), as Iliad 9.460; Callistratus read χάρις, 'pleasure' at the sight (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.29)
'spreads among men', rising as it were from those near at hand to the public; no exact parallel for the construction (Merry on 6.29)

30.n: with φάτις (29), held over to the head of the line
title of honor: πότνια μήτηρ 'lady mother'

31.p: verb · fut. part. act. nom. pl. fem.
31.n: future participle of purpose, uncontracted (Attic πλυνοῦσαι)
= ἅμα; ἅμʼ ἠοῖ φαινομένηφι 'when dawn appears', as Iliad 9.682

31.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. sg. fem.
31.n: epic -φι ending, here dative: 'with dawn appearing'

32.n: epic τοι = σοι; dative with ἅμʼ ἕψομαι

'fellow-worker, helper' (cf. ἔριθοι 'hired laborers', Iliad 18.550), in apposition to ἐγώ; only here in Homer; the scholia connect it with ἔρια 'wool', Merry with the root of ἄρω, ἀρτύω (Merry on 6.32)
= ἅμα; ἅμʼ ἕψομαι + dat. 'go along with'

33.n: short-vowel aorist subjunctive (= ἐντύνῃ), with long υ and -εαι in one syllable (Merry on 6.33); middle 'get yourself ready'

35.n: 'where': among the Phaeacians; or, as Merry prefers from the order of the words, taking up δῆμον (34): she is wooed by the noblest of her own land (Merry on 6.35)
epic τοι = σοι; dative of possession: 'you have your birth'
'family, kin'; the Harleian manuscript reads γένος ἐσσὶ καὶ αὐτή, 'you too belong to them by birth'; Merry prefers ἐστί … αὐτῇ, as printed (Merry's critical note and note on 6.35)

36.n: ἠῶθι πρό 'early, at first light', πρό adverbial, as 5.469, Iliad 11.50

37.n: feminine, as αἱ (83) and τάς (89) show
Homeric ἄμαξα = Attic ἅμαξα: a four-wheeled cart, as against the two-wheeled ἅρμα (Merry on 6.37); the ἀπήνη of 57
the wagon; accented before enclitic κεν
epic = ἄν; with the subjunctive in a relative clause of purpose

38.n: 'girdle, belt' (ζώννυμι 'gird'); only here in Homer; second accent from enclitic τε

39.n: comparative of καλός; ἐστί understood: 'it is more seemly'
epic ἠέ = ἤ, after the comparative

40.n: governs πόληος at the end of the line
basins or tanks for washing clothes, as Iliad 22.153 (Merry on 6.40); see 86–92

41.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

42.n: = Οὔλυμπόνδε: Οὔλυμπον (epic Οὔλυμπος, metrical lengthening of Ὄλυμπος) with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word (the Iliad prints Οὔλυμπον δέ, Iliad 1.425)

ὅθι φασί as Iliad 2.783, 24.615, of places known by report; strange of the gods' home, it led Köchly and others to think the description of Olympus a later insertion, which Merry thinks too strong a conclusion, though the lines may be suspect (Merry on 6.42)

43.n: = οὔτε; οὔτε … οὔτε … οὔτε 'neither … nor … nor'

44.n: 'draws near, comes upon' (πίλναμαι 'approach', Iliad 19.93); the compound only here in Homer
'clear sky, fair weather'; Rhianus read αἰθήρ (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.44)

45.n: 'is outspread', as πέπτατο δʼ αὐγή Iliad 17.371 (Merry on 6.45)
ἀ- + νεφέλη 'cloud'; two-termination adjective; only here in Homer; the summit stands clear above the clouds that elsewhere hang on snowy Olympus (Merry on 6.42)
perfect (δέδρομα) with present sense: 'is spread over'; again 20.357 (of mist)

46.n: the seat (ἕδος, 42); Rhianus read τῇ, referring it to the gleam (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.46)
epic ἐνί = ἐν; after its noun, accent thrown back (anastrophe)

47.n: used alone, as a name of Athena
reduplicated aorist (πέφραδον), augmented after the preverb: 'made plain'; without an object here, with πάντα at Iliad 20.340 (Merry on 6.47)

48.n: Ionic Ἠώς = Attic Ἕως; the goddess, here the morning itself
epic ἐϋ- = εὐ-; two-termination; epithet of Dawn, as Iliad 8.565
'who', i.e. and she; accented before enclitic μιν
unaugmented (= ἤγειρε); aorist and imperfect have the same form

49.n: = ἀπεθαύμασε: ἀπό intensive, 'was lost in wonder at' (Merry on 6.49); only here in Homer

50.n: unaugmented root aorist (= ἔβη); βῆ δʼ ἰέναι 'set out to go'
some read κατά (Merry's critical note on 6.50)
= δώματα, aspirated before ἵνʼ; plural for one house

optative in -ειε; of purpose after a past tense

51.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. masc.
51.n: epic ἐών = ὤν: 'found them (being) at home'

52.n: the mother, answered by τῷ δέ (53), the father
epic dat. pl. -οισι; with γυναιξίν, 'women who are handmaids'
in apposition; σὺν ἀμφιπόλοισι γυναιξίν again 80

53.n: 'the wool on the distaff, yarn', spun off from the ἠλακάτη 'distaff' (Iliad 6.491); found only in the plural (Merry on 6.53); ἠλάκατα στρωφῶσʼ ἁλιπόρφυρα again 306

53.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
53.n: = στρωφῶσα, contracted; frequentative of στρέφω 'turn': turning the wool from the distaff, i.e. spinning
'sea-purple': dyed with the purple of the sea (the murex), or purple like the sea (Merry on 6.53); again 306, 13.108
θύρα with the suffix -ζε 'to': 'to the door', i.e. out

54.p: verb · pres. part. mid. dat. sg. masc.

54.n: epic root aorist middle (ξυν- = συν-), unaugmented, + dat.: she hurried down the hall and caught him at the door (Merry on 6.54)
'to join, going after'; μετὰ βασιλῆας ἐς βουλήν as ἐς Ὠκεανὸν μετʼ ἀμύμονας Αἰθιοπῆας Iliad 1.423 (Merry on 6.54)
epic acc. pl. -ῆας; the Phaeacian lords, twelve beside Alcinous (8.390–391)

56.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

57.n: a child's word for father (cf. παππάζουσιν Iliad 5.408); only here in Homer
with the optative ἐφοπλίσσειας: a tentative, beseeching question, 'could you not get me ready …?' (Merry on 6.57)
epic -σσ-; optative in -ειας; the same question, οὐκ ἂν δή μοι ἄμαξαν ἐφοπλίσσαιτε, is Priam's angry command at Iliad 24.263: the tone lies in the context
a four-wheeled cart for loads, like the ἄμαξα of 37, generally drawn by mules or oxen (Merry on 6.57)

58.n: epic ἐϋ- = εὐ-; two-termination; of a wagon 'with good wheels' (κύκλος 'wheel'), of shields 'well-rounded' (Iliad 5.453)

59.p: verb · fut. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
verb · pf. part. pass. nom. pl. neut.
59.n: perfect passive of ῥυπόω 'soil' (ῥύπος 'dirt', 93), reduplicated ῥε- for the usual ἐρρ-, for the meter (Merry on 6.59); only here in Homer
singular verb with neuter plural subject

60.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

61.n: cognate accusative: βουλὰς βουλεύειν 'take counsel', as Iliad 10.147 (Merry on 6.61)

61.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.

62.n: epic 3rd-decl. plural υἷες; three of them, Laodamas, Halius and Clytoneus, are named at 8.118–119

63.n: οἱ δύʼ … τρεῖς δʼ: 'two of them … three …'

63.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

63.n: unmarried youths; printed without the diaeresis

63.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

64.n: 'newly washed' (νέος + πλύνω); only here in Homer

64.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. pl. masc.

65.n: perfect with present sense, singular with neuter plural subject: as the only daughter she bears this part of the household care, said half in play (Merry on 6.65)

66.n: = ἔφατο; middle form with active meaning
unaugmented, from epic αἴδομαι (= αἰδέομαι); + inf.
'in the bloom of youth', transferred from the young to the marriage, or a fixed epithet, 'fruitful' (Merry on 6.66)
the reason Athena had urged in the dream (Merry on 6.66)

68.n: epic τοι = σοι; φθονέω τινί τινος 'grudge someone something'

69.n: contracted -ευ (= ἔρχεο, Attic ἔρχου): 'away then!' (Merry on 6.69)

70.n: 'upper part' (ὑπέρτερος): a box for baggage, as the scholia take it, or a movable hood or awning, which ἀραρυῖαν makes Merry think the likelier (Merry on 6.70); only here in Homer

70.p: verb · pf. part. act. acc. sg. fem.

71.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

71.n: augmented reduplicated aorist of κέλομαι 'urge, call on'; + dat.

72.n: two-termination adjective; ἄμαξαν ἐύτροχον ἡμιονείην as Iliad 24.189

73.n: a by-form of ὁπλίζω 'make ready'; only here in Homer
= τε; τ → θ before rough breathing
unaugmented (= ὑπῆγον): brought them up and under the yoke (Merry on 6.73)
unaugmented (= ἔζευξαν); second accent from enclitic θʼ; ζεῦξαι δʼ ὑπʼ ὄχεσφιν Iliad 23.130 (Merry on 6.73)
= τε; τ → θ before rough breathing

74.n: unaugmented (= ἔφερε); Aristophanes read φέρον and κατέθηκαν (75), with the slaves as subject (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.74–75)
a fixed epithet, though the clothes are dirty, like σιγαλόεντα (26) (Merry on 6.26)

75.n: epic ἐϋ- = εὐ-: 'well-smoothed' (ξέω 'scrape, plane'); two-termination here (ἐϋξέστης … ἀπήνης Iliad 24.275)

76.n: = μενοεικέα: 'suited to the heart's desire' (μένος + ἔοικα); two-termination

77.n: 'cooked food, relish' eaten with bread, as 3.480
in tmesis: ἐν … τίθει; unaugmented, as from τιθέω (= ἐνετίθει)

78.n: 'skin, wineskin'; ἀσκῷ ἐν αἰγείῳ as Iliad 3.247

79.n: unaugmented (= ἔδωκεν); the mother; the line again 215, with δῶκαν

'oil flask'; in Homer only here and 215

80.g: she might bathe and anoint herself

81.n: μάστιγα καὶ ἡνία σιγαλόεντα as Iliad 5.226

82.n: unaugmented (= ἐμάστιξεν); μάστιξεν δʼ ἐλάαν as 3.484, Iliad 5.366
epic ἐλάαν (= ἐλᾶν, from ἐλάω = ἐλαύνω); infinitive of purpose: 'to drive on'
of the hooves and the wagon
epic gen./dat. dual -οιιν: the pair of mules

83.n: 'unceasingly': at a steady pace rather than a fast one, for the maids followed on foot (Merry on 6.83); 'raging without end' Iliad 4.440
unaugmented (= ἐτανύοντο); middle 'strained', at full stretch, as of horses Iliad 16.375

84.n: with αὐτήν (83); the line after 1.331 (οὐκ οἴη, ἅμα τῇ γε καὶ ἀμφίπολοι δύʼ ἕποντο)

86.n: tanks dug beside the river, with the water passing in and out of them (Merry on 6.86)

a field grass, taken as clover, couch grass, or dog's-tooth grass (Merry on 6.90); only here in Homer

epic dat. pl. -οισι; 'pits, trenches', presumably the washing troughs (86)

unaugmented (= ἐκάθηραν); second accent from enclitic τε

94.n: epic relative adverb (= ᾗ); ἧχι μάλιστα 'just where' (Merry on 6.94)

96.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. pl. fem.

100.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. fem.

epic οὔρεα (Attic ὄρη); Merry prints κατʼ οὔρεος 'down from the mountain', with the variant οὔρεα, which a scholion calls better and Kayser takes for Aristarchus' reading (Merry's critical note on 6.102)

103.n: Ionic Τηΰγετος (Attic Ταΰγετος): the range in the west of Laconia, running north to south to Cape Taenarum, its slopes covered with pine forest (Merry on 6.102); only here in Homer
= περιμήκης 'very tall'; two-termination adjective, as Iliad 14.287
a high range between Arcadia, Achaea and Elis, haunt of the boar that Heracles killed, whence κάπροισι (104) (Merry on 6.102); only here in Homer

104.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.

104.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; feminine, as ὠκείῃς shows: hinds

105.n: = τε; 'epic τε' in a simile; τ → θ before rough breathing

106.n: 'haunting the fields' (ἀγρός + νέμομαι), accented on the penult, active in sense (Merry on 6.106); Megaclides read the line ἀγρόμεναι παίζουσιν ἀνὰ δρία παιπαλόεντα (scholia, in Merry's critical note); only here in Homer
'sport', with the sense of hunting (Merry on 6.106)
perfect with present sense; γέγηθε δέ τε φρένα as Iliad 8.559 (the shepherd)

107.n: epic gen. pl. -άων; genitive with ὑπέρ

with ἔχει: 'holds above' (ὑπερέχω in tmesis), + gen. πασάων; Merry prefers 'lifts her head above all', as ὑψοῦ δὲ κάρη ἔχει Iliad 6.509, while Iliad 3.210 supports 'overtops them all by head and brow' (Merry on 6.107)

108.n: 'easily known' (ἀρι- intensive + γιγνώσκω); with ῥεῖα: 'easy to know', as ἀρίγνωτοι … θεοί Iliad 13.72

109.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; dative with μετέπρεπε
'untamed' (= ἄδμητος), of mules 'unbroken' (4.637), of a girl 'unwed'; two-termination; again 228

110.n: δὴ ἄρʼ with unusual hiatus (Merry on 6.110)
+ inf.: she was thinking of going home; the yoking and folding (111) are not done until 252 (Merry on 6.110)
οἶκον (οἶκος 'house') with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word

111.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
111.n: = ζεύξασα; with πτύξασα it defines νέεσθαι (110): she meant to go home once the mules were yoked and the clothes folded, which she does only at 252–253 (Merry on 6.110)

111.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

113.n: of purpose, with the optative after the past ἐνόησε
thematic aorist middle ἠγρόμην 'woke' (ἔγρετο 117); optative of purpose
'fair-faced' (εὖ + ὤψ 'face'); in Homer only of Nausicaa, here and 142

114.n: accented before enclitic οἱ; relative clause of purpose with the optative: 'who should be guide for him' (Merry on 6.114)

115.n: 'ball', as 100; in Homer only in the Odyssey (again 8.372, 8.377)
= ἔπειτα: 'so then', the first step in carrying out Athena's plan (Merry on 6.115)
fem. of βασιλεύς, 'queen' (4.697, of Penelope); here the king's daughter, Nausicaa

116.n: unaugmented (= ἥμαρτε), + gen.; Nausicaa is the subject, as of ἔμβαλε (Merry on 6.116)

unaugmented (= ἐνέβαλε), + dat.; Wolf restored ἔμβαλε from Eustathius and the Harleian scholia; others read ἔμπεσε 'it fell into', which Nitzsch thought the original reading (Merry's critical note on 6.116)

117.n: with ἄυσαν: 'they cried aloud thereat' (Merry on 6.117), as ἐπὶ δʼ αὐτὸς ἄυσε Iliad 15.321

118.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

118.n: κατὰ φρένα καὶ κατὰ θυμόν as 4.120 and Iliad 1.193

119.n: αὖτε in an impatient question, 'now again!' (Merry on 6.119, after Ebeling)
present with perfect sense: 'am I come'

120.n: ἦ introducing a direct question, answered by ἦε (121): 'are they … or …?'; supply εἰσί
the people of the land; accented before enclitic γʼ
'men of violence, outrageous' (ὕβρις); used as an adjective

121.n: epic ἠέ = ἤ, the second member of the question begun with ἦ (120)
'loving strangers, hospitable' (φίλος + ξεῖνος); in Homer only in this line (again 8.576, 9.176, 13.202)
'and': καί σφιν νόος ἐστί 'and they have a mind', rendered 'with a mind'; accented before enclitic σφιν
epic σφι(ν) = αὐτοῖς; dative of possession

'god-fearing' (θεός + δέος), as Buttmann explained it, against the older view that it is a form of θεοειδής; Düntzer and a scholium took it as 'god-pleasing'; here it spells out φιλόξεινοι, men who fear the wrath of Zeus, god of strangers (Merry on 6.121); in Homer only in the Odyssey

122.n: ὥς τε 'as it were', to be joined with κουράων: 'as it were the voice of girls' (Merry on 6.122, comparing 4.45); accented before enclitic τε
Ionic κούρη = κόρη; epic gen. pl. -άων; defined further by νυμφάων (123), as ἀνδρῶν … βασιλήων 4.63 (Merry on 6.122)
epic aorist ἀμφήλυθον (ἀμφί + ἤλυθον = ἦλθον): 'came round, surrounded'; in Homer only here and 12.369
'female'; the form in -υς serves for the feminine, with ἀυτή
'shout, cry', in the Iliad mostly the war cry

123.n: epic gen. pl. -άων; in apposition to κουράων (122); 123–124 are accepted by the scholia but suspected by many modern editors (Merry on 6.122)
lit. 'heads'; ὀρέων αἰπεινὰ κάρηνα as Iliad 20.58

124.n: '(water-)meadows'; in Homer only in this line, which = Iliad 20.9 (and the Hymn to Aphrodite 99), as Nitzsch noted (Merry on 6.122); there too of the nymphs

125.n: interrogative particle, as the text is printed: 'Am I perhaps …?'; the scholiast wrote the disjunctive ἤ 'or', the alternative to the nymphs of 122–124 (Merry on 6.122); some editions end the line with a full stop (Merry's critical note on 6.125)
'with human speech' (αὐδή): mortal men, as against the nymphs; αὐδήεσσα of Ino, 5.334

126.n: Ionic -η-; more likely a future of plain statement, followed by the subjunctive of intention ἴδωμαι, than a short-vowel aorist subjunctive parallel to it (Merry on 6.126)
middle of εἶδον, same sense; hortatory subjunctive: 'let me see'

127.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

127.n: genitive of separation with ὑπεδύσετο, implying escape, as κακῶν ὑποδύσεαι 20.53 (Merry on 6.127)
mixed aorist (σ-stem with thematic endings); he had crept in under the bushes at 5.481–482

128.n: 'young branch, shoot'; πτόρθον … φύλλων 'a branch of leaves', a loose genitive of material (Merry on 6.128); only here in Homer

129.n: genitive of material with πτόρθον (Merry on 6.128)
of purpose, with the optative after the past κλάσε
'shield, protect': 'that girt about his body it might cover his nakedness' (Merry on 6.129)
μήδεα 'the private parts', a different sense from μήδεα 'counsels', in Homer only here and 18.67, 18.87, 22.476

130.n: epic infinitive = ἰέναι: βῆ δʼ ἴμεν 'set off to go', 'went on'; the half-line as Iliad 12.299
ὥς τε 'just as', introducing a simile; accented before enclitic τε
'reared in the mountains' (ὄρος + τρέφω); λέων ὀρεσίτροφος as Iliad 12.299, 17.61
epic dat. ἀλκί, as from a root noun (= ἀλκῇ); only here in the Odyssey, five times in the Iliad, always with πεποιθώς

130.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
130.n: perfect πέποιθα 'trust' + dat.; ἀλκὶ πεποιθώς as Iliad 17.61

131.n: = τε; 'epic τε' after a relative in a simile

131.p: verb · pres. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
131.n: passive of ὕω 'rain'; Nitzsch compares νιφόμενος 'snowed upon' in Xenophon, Hellenica 2.4.3 (Merry on 6.131); only here in Homer

131.p: verb · pres. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.
131.n: passive of ἄημι 'blow', as ἄητο Iliad 21.386 (Merry on 6.131)
adverbial: 'within', in his head, as ἐν δέ οἱ ὄσσε Iliad 19.16
dual 'the two eyes', here with the singular δαίεται, as Iliad 12.466 (Merry on 6.131)

132.n: δαίω 'kindle', middle 'blaze'; singular verb with the dual ὄσσε (131); not δαίομαι 'divide' (δαίεται 'is torn', 1.48)

+ dat. 'goes among' cattle and sheep, raiding the farmyard, but μετʼ … ἐλάφους (133), + acc., of pursuing the flying deer (Merry on 6.132); Eustathius preferred the reading ἐπέρχεται (Merry's critical note on 6.132)

133.n: 'belly', i.e. hunger: Merry compares 'suadet enim vesana fames', Virgil, Aeneid 9.340 (Merry on 6.133)

134.p: verb · fut. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
134.n: future participle of purpose, agreeing with ἑ (133); + gen. 'make trial of, attack'; the line = Iliad 12.301

135.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); dative with μίξεσθαι (136)
two-termination adjective; epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); κούρῃσιν ἐυπλοκάμοισι again 222
'was fain', + fut. inf.: the point of the simile is that lion and man alike are driven by hunger into unusual boldness, χρειὼ γὰρ ἵκανε (136) (Merry on 6.135)

136.n: future infinitive with ἔμελλε (135): 'to go among', + dat. κούρῃσιν

136.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

137.p: verb · pf. part. mid./pass. nom. sg. masc.

138.n: unaugmented (= ἔτρεσαν), epic -σσ-: 'fled scared'; Aristarchus held that τρεῖν always means flight, which Merry doubts for some passages (Merry on 6.138)
ἄλλυδις ἄλλη 'one this way, another that'
with ἄλλυδις: each girl a different way
'beach, shore'; here 'jutting spits', probably of low sandy beach near the river mouth (Merry on 6.138)

138.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. pl. fem.

139.n: Nausicaa's father, king of the Phaeacians (12)

140.n: θάρσος ἐνὶ φρεσὶ θῆκε as 3.76–77, of Telemachus
in tmesis with εἵλετο (ἐξαιρέω 'take out, take away') (Merry on 6.140)

141.p: verb · aor. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.
141.n: 2nd aorist middle: 'having checked herself' from flight, as Eustathius explains, rather than 'holding (her veil) before her' as at 1.334 (Merry on 6.141)
unaugmented aorist (= ἐμερμήριξε); + ἤ … ἦ (142–143): 'was divided whether … or'

142.n: epic γούνων (= γονάτων); genitive of the part grasped, with λαβών
optative in an indirect deliberative question after the past μερμήριξεν

142.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
142.n: 'taking (her) by the knees', the suppliant's gesture

143.n: second member of ἤ … ἦ 'whether … or', accented ἦ; not ἦ 'truly'
'just as he was', defined further by ἀποσταδά (Merry on 6.143)
'standing aloof' (ἀφίσταμαι), = ἀποσταδόν (Iliad 15.556); in Homer only here and 146
epic dat. pl. -οισι; agrees with ἐπέεσσιν; 143–144 and 146 'with soothing words', as Iliad 6.343

144.n: = λίσσοιτο; the verse was suspected by Athenocles, a pupil of Aristarchus, for the repeated λίσσοιτο and because the question is only whether to clasp her knees or speak from a distance (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.144)
'in the hope that', with the optative

145.p: verb · pres. part. act. dat. sg. masc.

145.n: aor. δοάσσατο 'seemed' (with κέρδιον εἶναι), a defective verb; the line = 5.474

146.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; agrees with ἐπέεσσιν

147.n: + optative after the past δοάσσατο (145); accented before enclitic οἱ

147.p: verb · aor. part. act. dat. sg. masc.
147.n: agrees with οἱ; conditional: 'if he took'

148.n: 'crafty, shrewd' (κέρδος 'gain'): words from κέρδος range from a goddess' wise counsel to Agamemnon's greed (κερδαλεόφρων, Iliad 1.149) (Merry on 6.148)

149.n: 'entreat', properly 'clasp the knees' (γόνυ), here said from a distance; contracted from -όομαι; second accent from enclitic σε
'queen, lady': elsewhere in Homer used only of goddesses, Demeter (Iliad 14.326) and Athena (3.380), a special compliment (Merry on 6.149); again 175
printed ἦ, as Ptolemy of Ascalon wrote it, making 'or are you a mortal?' a second question; others wrote ἤ, 'whether a goddess or a mortal' (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.149)
of either sex: here of a woman, as 5.334

150.n: answered by εἰ δέ (153); accent from enclitic τις
'some goddess'; the relative τοί then speaks of the gods at large
epic τοί = οἵ; article used as relative; τοὶ οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἔχουσιν as 5.169, again 243

151.n: dative with ἐίσκω (152); second accent from enclitic σε; Nausicaa among her maids was likened to Artemis at 102–109
in apposition to Ἀρτέμιδι; Διὸς κούρῃ μεγάλοιο again 323, of Athena

152.n: accusative of respect; second accent from enclitic τε; the half-line as Iliad 2.58
τε … τε … τε: 'in looks and stature and build'
accusative of respect; second accent from enclitic τε

153.n: answers εἰ μέν (150); accent from enclitic τις
partitive with τις; εἰ δέ τίς ἐσσι βροτῶν as Iliad 6.142
epic τοί = οἵ; article used as relative

154.n: τρὶς μάκαρες 'three times blessed', as 5.306; Merry's text prints τρισμάκαρες as one word
dative of possession; accented (emphatic) before enclitic γε

155.n: epic σφισι = αὐτοῖς; dative of possession, though the participle λευσσόντων (157) is genitive (Merry on 6.157)

156.n: 'good cheer' (εὖ + φρήν); epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν), a plural of the abstract noun, as ἀεσιφροσύνῃσιν 15.470 (Merry on 6.156); the scholia reject a reading ἐν εὐφροσύνῃσιν (Merry's critical note on 6.156)

157.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. pl. masc.
157.n: genitive, though σφισι (155) is dative: a loose construction, on the way to the genitive absolute (Merry on 6.157)

157.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. fem.
157.n: Ionic contraction -εῦσαν (= -έουσαν); εἰσοιχνέω 'go into' (οἰχνέω 'go'), in Homer only here and 9.120; feminine by sense, with the neuter θάλος (Merry on 6.157)

158.n: adverbial 'exceedingly', with κῆρι a locative dative, as 5.36 (Merry on 6.158)
superlative of μάκαρ, 'most blessed', with the genitive ἄλλων, as 5.105 (Merry on 6.158); again 11.483

159.n: κε + subjunctive: 'whoever'; accent from enclitic σʼ
= σε; object of ἀγάγηται, not of βρίσας (Merry on 6.159)
epic ἔεδνα = ἕδνα, the suitor's gifts (1.277); instrumental

159.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
159.n: 'prevailing' (βρίθω 'be heavy'): outweighing the other suitors by the number of his gifts, as Eustathius explains; βρίθω is intransitive in Homer, so σʼ is the object of ἀγάγηται (Merry on 6.159)
= οἶκόνδε: οἶκος with the directional suffix -δε, 'homeward'
reduplicated aorist ἤγαγον; middle 'lead home' as a bride; subjunctive with κε in a general relative clause

160.n: with βροτόν; editors emend (Bekker τοῖον ϝεῖδον, La Roche τοιόνδε ἴδον; Merry's critical note on 6.160)

161.n: = οὔτε; οὔτε … οὔτε 'neither … nor'; the line as 4.142, where Helen speaks (εἰσορόωσαν)
'awe, amazement'; σέβας μʼ ἔχει εἰσορόωντα as 3.123, 4.75

161.p: verb · pres. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
161.n: epic diectasis (= εἰσορῶντα); agrees with μʼ

162.n: locative dative; the island of Apollo, in Homer named only here; Merry places the visit on the voyage from Aulis to Troy (Merry on 6.162)

163.n: the date palm, a homograph of φοῖνιξ 'purple'; in Homer only here; a palm in Apollo's precinct at Delos was still shown in Cicero's day (Cicero, Laws 1.1.2; Merry on 6.162)

163.p: verb · pres. part. mid. acc. sg. neut.

165.n: cognate accusative with ἦλθον (164), like βουλὰς βουλεύειν 61 (Merry on 6.164)
unaugmented (= ἔμελλεν), the reading of most manuscripts; a scholium of Aristonicus, as Merry corrects it, says that Homer does not use the later Attic ἤμελλεν (Merry's critical note on 6.165)
dative of possession: 'were to be mine'
= κήδεα, uncontracted (Attic κήδη); subject of ἔσεσθαι

166.n: ὣς δʼ αὔτως 'and in the same way' (in Homer always parted by δέ); it answers ὡς (168), the comparison taken in reverse order (Merry on 6.166)
epic κεῖνος = ἐκεῖνος: the palm shoot; not elided before ἰδών (originally ϝιδ-)

166.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

166.n: pluperfect of τέθηπα 'be astounded' (aor. ταφών), Ionic 1 sg. -εα (Attic -η)

167.n: governs γαίης, parted from it by δόρυ: neither an adverb nor tmesis, but a licence unusual in Homer, as δήεις δʼ ἐν πήματα οἴκῳ 11.115 (Merry on 6.167)

168.n: 'marvel at, wonder at', as Iliad 3.181, not 'begrudge' (as 5.119); second accent from enclitic τε
perfect with present sense 'be astounded', with σε; second accent from enclitic τε
perfect δείδια with present sense (Attic δέδοικα)

169.n: epic γούνων (= γονάτων); genitive with ἅψασθαι
present with perfect sense: 'is come upon'

170.n: adjective with the force of the adverb χθές, as 2.262 (Merry on 6.170)
epic ἐεικοστός = εἰκοστός; with ἤματι, dative of time

171.n: 'for so long', the whole twenty days (Merry on 6.171)
contracted (-εε > -ει); singular verb with the nearer subject κῦμα

172.n: = ἀπό; placed between noun and adjective

apocope and assimilation: κάββαλε = κατέβαλε (some manuscripts κάμβαλε); the object (με) understood from 171; 'cast me ashore', thrown out by the winds, not a safe landing, as the scholia say (Merry on 6.172)

173.n: 'still, yet more'; Merry's text reads ὄφρα τί που
καὶ τῇδε 'here too', as in all his other trials (Merry on 6.173)
dat. fem. of ὅδε used as adverb: 'here'

174.n: = παύσεσθαι; middle 'cease'; the subject, his suffering, is understood
used as a noun: 'many things', evils
epic future without σ (= τελοῦσι), the same form as the present
= πάροιθε with movable ν: 'ere that', before his troubles end, not 'hereafter' as a scholium takes it (Merry on 6.174)

175.n: not elided: ἄνασσα once began with ϝ (ϝάνασσα), as 3.380
governed by ἐς (176): σὲ … ἐς πρώτην = ἐς σὲ πρώτην, the pronoun put first for emphasis, to balance τῶν δʼ ἄλλων (Merry on 6.175)

175.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

176.n: Ionic ἐς = εἰς; of persons, as Iliad 7.312 εἰς Ἀγαμέμνονα (Merry on 6.175)

177.n: here without a sharp distinction from ἄστυ (178), though πόλις points to a settled community, ἄστυ to the dwellings (Merry on 6.177); πόλιν καὶ γαῖαν ἔχουσιν again 195

178.n: originally ϝάστυ 'dwelling-place' (Merry on 6.177); ἄστυ … δεῖξον answered by ἄστυ … δείξω (194)
'rag, ragged cloth'; in Homer only in the Odyssey
middle 'put around oneself'; infinitive of purpose

179.n: with εἴλυμα; accent from enclitic που
'wrapper' (εἰλύω 'wrap'): a cover of coarse cloth for packing the clothes, so that his request is a very modest one (Merry on 6.179); only here in Homer
'pieces of cloth', here the clothes brought to be washed: εἴλυμα σπείρων 'a wrapper of the linen' (Merry on 6.179)

179.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

180.n: τόσα … ὅσα 'as much as', i.e. all

181.n: 'like-mindedness, concord' (ὁμόφρων); in Homer only here and 15.198
Aeolic-epic optative in -ειαν; optative of wish

182.n: genitive of comparison, spelled out by ἢ ὅτε (183), a pleonastic ἤ after the genitive (Merry on 6.182)
comparative related to κράτος 'strength'; supply ἐστί

183.n: after the comparatives, explaining τοῦ (182) (Merry on 6.182)
= ὅτε; τ → θ before rough breathing

183.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. du. masc.
183.n: dual: husband and wife; uncontracted -έο-; 'being like-minded', in Homer only here and 9.456
dual, with ἀνὴρ ἠδὲ γυνή (184); subjunctive after ὅτε without κε, in a general statement; οἶκον ἔχειν 'keep house'

184.n: uncontracted (Attic ἄλγη); accusative in apposition to the whole clause (Merry on 6.184)
epic dat. pl. -εσσι; used as a noun

185.n: 'well-wisher' (εὐμενής), the opposite of δυσμενής; epic dat. pl. -ῃσι; only here in Homer
= τε; 'epic τε' in a general statement
gnomic aorist: 'hear', here 'perceive, know', as the scholia explain, comparing μάλιστα δὲ καὐτὸς ἀνέγνω, Iliad 13.734; the use is strange, and Nauck thought the words corrupt (Merry on 6.185)

187.n: its main clause is οὔτʼ οὖν ἐσθῆτος (192), after the parenthesis 188–190 and a second ἐπεί clause (191) (Merry on 6.187)

188.n: 'prosperity, happiness'; the point lies in ὅπως ἐθέλῃσιν (189), the arbitrary dealing of good and evil, as 4.237 (Merry on 6.188)

189.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); used as a noun
epic subj. -ῃσι(ν); subjunctive in a general clause without κε

190.n: = τάδε: 'these hardships which I see' (Merry on 6.190)
epic perfect infinitive -άμεν (= τετληκέναι); χρὴ τετλάμεν ἔμπης as 3.209

191.n: present with perfect sense: 'you are come'

192.n: 'so then', marking the main clause after the clauses with ἐπεί (187, 191)
uncontracted -εαι (= δευήσῃ); epic δεύομαι = δέομαι 'lack', + gen.

193.n: genitive, with μὴ δεύεσθαι understood from δευήσεαι: 'which it is right that a suppliant should not lack' (Merry on 6.193)
= ἐπέοικε (κ → χ before rough breathing); impersonal: 'it is fitting'; the line again 14.511
'much-suffering': Aristarchus took it as = ταλαίπωρος, others as 'come from afar' (scholia on 7.24, in Merry on 6.193); in Homer only in the Odyssey

193.p: verb · aor. part. act. acc. sg. masc.
193.n: 'meeting (us)', with a sense of sudden need (Merry on 6.193); a manuscript reading ἀντιάσασθαι is probably a late correction (Merry's critical note on 6.193)

196.n: epic gen. -οιο; θυγάτηρ μεγαλήτορος Ἀλκινόοιο as 17 and 213

197.n: Alcinous; governed by ἐκ, which follows it: 'and on him … depend'
with τοῦ: ἐκ τοῦ ἔχεται 'depends on him', as ἐκ σέο ἄρτηται in Herodotus 6.109 (Merry on 6.197)
middle 'hang on, depend on'; singular verb with the two subjects
epic κάρτος (metathesis) = κράτος; κάρτος τε βίη τε as 4.415

198.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); dative with κέλευσε
two-termination adjective; epic dat. pl. -οισι; ἀμφιπόλοισιν ἐυπλοκάμοισι again 238

199.n: root aorist ἔστην, intransitive: 'halt'; second accent from enclitic μοι

199.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. pl. fem.

200.n: ἦ μή που, like Attic ἆρα μή, asks a question expecting the answer 'no': 'you don't mean that you think …?' (Merry on 6.200)
subject of ἔμμεναι; partitive with δυσμενέων … ἀνδρῶν
δυσμενέων … ἀνδρῶν, as ἀνδράσι δυσμενέεσσιν Iliad 6.453
= φάσθε; middle with active sense: 'think, suppose'

201.n: = ἐστί (τ → θ before the rough breathing of οὗτος): 'exists'
not Odysseus: it introduces a general statement, 'that man', as οὐκ ἔσθʼ οὗτος ἀνήρ 16.437 (Merry on 6.201, 6.206)

disputed: 'living', so Aristarchus by the scholia, with διερὸς βροτός the predicate ('that man is not alive …'), the rendering Merry prefers; others 'fleeing, timid' (δίεσθαι, δέος), in apposition to οὗτος ἀνήρ; Callistratus read δυερός 'wretched' (Merry on 6.201); again 9.43, διερῷ ποδί
epic subjunctive with future sense in a negative statement, as οὐδὲ ἴδωμαι Iliad 1.262 (Merry on 6.201)

202.n: aorist ἱκόμην; subjunctive with κεν in a relative clause of future sense

203.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

203.n: used as a noun; epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν)

204.n: 'loud-dashing' (πολύς + κλύζω 'dash, wash'); πολυκλύστῳ ἐνὶ πόντῳ as 4.354
epic ἐνί = ἐν; ἐνὶ πόντῳ means only that the land lies far across the sea, not that Scheria is an island (Merry on 6.204)

205.n: 'at the ends' of the earth, as the Ethiopians, 1.23 (Merry on 6.205)
Aeolic ἄμμι = ἡμῖν; dative with ἐπιμίσγεται
middle 'mix with, have dealings with', + dat.

206.n: deictic, 'this man here', of Odysseus, unlike οὗτος (201) (Merry on 6.206)

206.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. masc.

207.n: + inf.; the subject accusative is understood
'sent by, from', and so 'under the protection of' Zeus (Merry on 6.207); πρὸς γὰρ Διός … φίλη τε (207–208) again 14.57–58

208.n: Ionic ξεῖνος = ξένος; second accent from enclitic τε
'beggar' (cf. πτώσσω 'cower'); second accent from enclitic τε; in Homer only in the Odyssey
'a gift, though small, is welcome': small to the giver, dear to the receiver, as a scholium explains; cf. ὀλίγον τε φίλον τε, Iliad 1.167 (Merry on 6.208)

209.n: ἀλλά with an imperative, 'but'; 'but come' would be ἀλλʼ ἄγε
second accent from enclitic τε; βρῶσίν τε πόσιν τε as 1.191, again 246, 248

210.n: second accent from enclitic τʼ; the object (him) understood
adverbial, 'thereat', as ἐπὶ σκέπας ἦν ἀνέμοιο 5.443
'shelter, cover', + gen. ἀνέμοιο 'from the wind'; in Homer only in the Odyssey

211.n: epic 3 pl. of the root aorist (= ἔστησαν), intransitive: 'halted'

212.n: epic κάδ = κατά (apocope, assimilated before δ); in tmesis with εἷσαν (καθίζω 'set down')
= Ὀδυσσῆα (epic acc. -ῆα), elided; Merry prints Ὀδυσσέα, with Ὀδυσσῆʼ as a variant (Merry's critical note on 6.212)
in tmesis: κὰδ … εἷσαν = καθεῖσαν; causative aorist εἷσα 'made sit': 'brought him to the sheltered spot and set him down there' (Merry on 6.212)
'to (the shelter)', with the motion implied in εἷσαν (Merry on 6.212)

214.n: epic πάρ = παρά; in tmesis with ἔθηκαν (παρατίθημι 'set beside'), + dat. οἱ
= εἵματα, in apposition to φᾶρος and χιτῶνα: 'for raiment' (Merry on 6.214)

215.n: unaugmented (= ἔδωκαν); the line as 79 (δῶκεν), of Nausicaa's mother
'oil flask'; in Homer only here and 79

216.n: thematic imperfect of ἄνωγα, as if from ἀνώγω
contracted (= λούεσθαι); middle 'bathe oneself', though Nausicaa had said λούσατε 'bathe him' (210) (Merry on 6.216)

217.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι; dative with μετηύδα

218.n: = στῆτε (τ → θ before the rough breathing of οὕτω)
'yonder': he shows the distance with a wave of the hand (Merry on 6.218)
'at a distance' (ἀπό + πρό with the suffix -θεν)

219.n: epic gen. du. -οιιν; genitive of separation
short-vowel aorist subjunctive (= ἀπολούσωμαι) after ὄφρα (218), the same form as the future; middle 'wash off myself'

220.n: short-vowel aorist subjunctive (= χρίσωμαι) after ὄφρα (218); middle 'anoint oneself'
'away from': literally 'for long the oil has been away from my skin'
enclitic; present with δηρόν: 'has long been (away)'

221.n: 'face to face, openly': in the handmaids' sight
epic λοέσσ- (from λοέω = λούω): future, or short-vowel aorist subjunctive (= λοέσσωμαι), with ἄν; middle 'bathe oneself'

222.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν); dative with μετελθών; κούρῃσιν ἐυπλοκάμοισι as 135

222.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
222.n: + dat. 'come among'; Eustathius has ἐπελθών (Merry's critical note on 6.222)

223.n: = ἔφατο (τ → θ before rough breathing); ὣς ἔφαθʼ, αἱ δʼ … as 211, 247
they told Nausicaa what he had said (218–222)

224.n: 'with water from' the river, as λόʼ ἐκ τρίποδος 10.361 (Merry on 6.224)
epic acc. χρόα (Attic χρῶτα); with ἅλμην (225) a double accusative, as with verbs of taking away (Merry on 6.224)

225.n: ἀμπέχω = ἀμφέχω (ἀμφί + ἔχω), unaugmented: 'covered, clung round'; only here in Homer

226.n: 'wipe, rub off'; only here in Homer
'scurf', the crust of dried salt; Merry connects it with κνάω 'scrape' and κόνις 'dust' (Merry on 6.226); only here in Homer
epic gen. -οιο; two-termination, with ἁλός; meaning disputed

227.n: unaugmented epic aorist λοεσσ- (from λοέω = λούω); middle 'bathe oneself'
= λίπα, elided: 'richly, thickly' (with oil); not λίπε from λείπω; as λίπʼ ἐλαίῳ 96 and 3.466 (Merry on 6.227)
unaugmented (= ἤλειψεν); the object, himself, understood

228.n: in tmesis with ἕσσαθʼ (ἀμφιέννυμι 'put on around')
= ἕσσατο (τ → θ before rough breathing); in tmesis with ἀμφί; aorist middle of ἕννυμι 'clothe', epic -σσ-
unaugmented aorist (= ἔπορε); no present attested
'unwedded' (ἀ- + δάμνημι 'tame'), of a girl; of animals 'unbroken' (Iliad 10.293); two-termination

229.n: Odysseus; τὸν μέν begins the main clause after ἐπεί (227) (Merry on 6.229)
unaugmented (= ἔθηκεν); 'made', with the predicates μείζονα and πάσσονα (230)

229.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
229.n: epic perfect participle (ἐκγέγονα): 'born of', 'child of', as Iliad 3.199

230.n: comparative of μέγας; second accent from enclitic τʼ; predicate with θῆκεν (229)
epic infinitive -έειν (= εἰσιδεῖν); infinitive of respect: 'to look at'
comparative πάσσων of παχύς 'thick, stout'; in Homer only in the Odyssey (again 8.20, 18.195, 23.157, 24.369)
epic κάδ = κατά (apocope, assimilated to δ); in tmesis with ἧκε (231: καθίημι 'let fall'), with the genitive κάρητος
gen. of κάρη (stem καρητ-); with κάδ: 'down from his head'

231.n: 'woolly, thick': the thick hair of a vigorous man (Merry on 6.231); a different word from οὖλος 'baneful'
in tmesis: κὰδ (230) … ἧκε = καθῆκε; κ-aorist ἧκα of ἵημι: 'let fall'
'of the hyacinth' (ὑάκινθος, Iliad 14.348); in Homer only here and 23.158; the point of the likeness, the dark color or the clustering curls, is disputed: Merry takes the curls (Merry on 6.231)
epic accentuation ὁμοῖος; + dat.; agrees with κόμας

232.n: simile, answered by ὣς (235); 232–234 = 23.159–161, and 235 nearly 23.162
ὡς δʼ ὅτε, a simile, with the subjunctive περιχεύεται
object of περιχεύεται: the gold is 'poured round' the silver
short-vowel aorist subjunctive (= περιχεύηται) of the epic aorist ἔχευα (Merry on 6.232); cf. χρυσὸν κέρασιν περιχεύας 3.384
the ground on which the gold is laid (Merry on 6.232)

233.n: 'knowing, skilled' (cf. οἶδα, ἄϊδρις 'ignorant'); in Homer only in the Odyssey (again 7.108, 23.160)
reduplicated aorist δέδαον 'taught', causative of ἐδάην 'learned'; + two accusatives, ὃν and τέχνην (234); singular with the first of two subjects
here patroness of all craftsmen, with Hephaestus, as in the Homeric Hymn to Hephaestus (Merry on 6.233)

234.n: Ionic -ην: 'art in all its branches' (Merry on 6.233)
epic τελείω = τελέω; the subject is ἀνήρ (232): the result of the gods' teaching, a clause later Greek would put with ὥστε (Merry on 6.234)

235.n: Odysseus: dative of the person, with κεφαλῇ … ὤμοις the parts
epic aorist ἔχευα: 'poured down, shed', + dat.; χάριν κατέχευε as 2.12; κατέχευε χάριν κεφαλῇ τε καὶ ὤμοις again 8.19; 23.162 has περίχευε

236.n: 'away (from the others)'; ἀπάνευθε κιὼν ἐπὶ θῖνα θαλάσσης as 2.260

236.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
236.n: epic verb 'go'; participle accented like an aorist

237.n: uncontracted dat. -εϊ; dative of respect; κάλλεϊ τε στίλβων Iliad 3.392, of Paris

237.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

237.n: Ionic θηέομαι = θεάομαι; unaugmented imperfect, contracted (from θηέετο)

238.n: δή ῥα τότε 'then indeed'; accent from enclitic ῥα
epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); ἀμφιπόλοισιν ἐυπλοκάμοισι as 198

239.n: root aorist imperative; second accent from enclitic μευ; κλῦτέ μευ is the scholia's reading, the manuscripts have κλῦτέ μοι (Merry's critical note on 6.239)
epic μευ = μου; genitive with verb of hearing

240.n: with ἀέκητι: 'not against the will', i.e. by the will of the gods, as οὔ σε θεῶν ἀέκητι 3.28 (Merry on 6.240)
'against the will of' (cf. ἀέκων), + gen. θεῶν

241.n: = Φαιήκεσσι, epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative with ἐπιμίσγεται

242.n: = δέατο 'seemed', perhaps an imperfect from a stem δεα-, beside δοα- in δοάσσατο (Iliad 13.458); only here in Homer (Merry on 6.242)

243.n: epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν); dative with ἔοικε
perfect with present sense: 'be like', + dat.
epic τοί = οἵ; article used as relative; τοὶ οὐρανὸν εὐρὺν ἔχουσιν as 150 and 1.67

244.n: αἲ γάρ + optative: a wish, 'would that'; epic αἰ = εἰ; Aristarchus athetized 244–245, hesitating over 244 because Alcman had adapted it (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.244–245)
dative of the person: 'a husband for me'

244.p: verb · pf. part. pass. nom. sg. masc.
244.n: with εἴη: 'be called'; Homer forms this periphrasis only with the perfect passive participle (Merry on 6.244, comparing Iliad 2.260)

245.p: verb · pres. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

245.n: Odysseus: set emphatically, it turns from such a husband to the man himself (Ameis, in Merry on 6.244)
2nd aorist (ἅδον, cf. εὔαδε) of ἁνδάνω 'please', + dat.; optative of wish, still with αἲ γάρ (244)

246.n: ἀλλά with an imperative, 'but'; the line = 209

247.n: the line as 3.477 (αἱ … τῆς for οἱ … τοῦ)

248.n: epic apocopated πάρ = παρά; in tmesis with ἔθεσαν (παρατίθημι 'set beside'), + dat. Ὀδυσσῆι
epic dat. -ῆϊ; its final ι is long before ἔθεσαν, though no digamma follows (Merry on 6.248)
second accent from enclitic τε; βρῶσίν τε πόσιν τε as 209, 246

249.n: ἦ τοι (= ἤτοι), like μέν, answered by αὐτάρ (251)
with πολύτλας δῖος Ὀδυσσεύς in apposition
imperfect of ἔσθω, by-form of ἐσθίω; in Homer only in this formula (5.94, here, 7.177)

250.n: 'greedily, eagerly' (cf. ἁρπάζω 'snatch'); the adverb in Homer only here and 14.110

251.n: = ἄλλο; ἄλλʼ ἐνόησε 'thought of another thing', as 112 and 2.382

252.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. fem.

252.n: = ἐπί, set between adjective and noun

253.n: 'with strong hoofs' (κρατερός + ὄνυξ); ἡμιόνους κρατερώνυχας as Iliad 24.277
epic ἄν = ἀνά; in tmesis with ἔβη (ἀναβαίνω 'mount')
root aorist; in tmesis: ἂν … ἔβη = ἀνέβη

254.n: aorist and imperfect have the same form
ἔπος τʼ ἔφατʼ ἔκ τʼ ὀνόμαζεν as 4.610, 5.181

255.n: mixed aorist (σ-stem with thematic ending) imperative: 'rise', as Iliad 3.250, + inf. ἴμεν (Merry on 6.255)
= πόλινδε, elided: πόλις with the suffix -δε 'to', printed as one word; πόλινδʼ ἴμεν as 7.14 (Merry on 6.255)
subjunctive of purpose with ὄφρα (the form is also the future)

256.n: subject of εἰδησέμεν (257); accented before enclitic φημι
enclitic; + acc. and inf.: 'I am sure, I promise'

257.n: future of οἶδα (εἰδήσω), epic -έμεν (= εἰδήσειν), after φημι (256); cf. εἰδήσεις … ὅσσον ἄρισται 7.327 (Merry on 6.257)

258.n: the line as 5.342, with ἔρδειν for ἔρξαι
parataxis: the clause gives the reason; accent from enclitic μοι

259.n: = ὄφρα; ὄφρʼ ἄν + subjunctive: 'as long as', answered by τόφρα (260)
with the subjunctive; ἄν and κε together, as 5.361
answered by αὐτάρ (262); accent from enclitic κʼ
accusative of the ground covered: 'while we are going along the fields' (Merry on 6.259)
short-vowel subjunctive (= ἴωμεν), with ὄφρʼ ἄν
= ἔργα: the tilled land, as Iliad 16.392

261.n: ὁδὸν ἡγεμονεύσω 'I will lead the way'

262.n: = ἐπεὶ ἄν; + subjunctive; the clause has no proper apodosis, the sentence being lost in the description: Merry finds it resumed only at 295 (Merry on 6.262)
epic gen. πόλιος (Attic πόλεως); genitive with ἐπιβήομεν 'set foot on', as πόληος … ἐπιβαινέμεν Iliad 16.395–396 (Merry on 6.262)

short-vowel subjunctive (= ἐπιβῶμεν); most manuscripts have ἐπιβείομεν (as 10.334); ἐπιβήομεν, which Merry thinks right, is in the scholia and a few manuscripts (Merry's critical note and note on 6.262)
follows its noun, accent thrown back (anastrophe)
'tower', here the towered wall as a whole, 'rampart', as Iliad 12.333; ἐστί understood

263.n: a harbor on each side of the narrow neck that joins the city to the land, as at Tyre (Merry on 6.263)

264.n: 'entrance' (εἰς + ἴθμα 'step', cf. εἶμι), the neck between the two harbors (Merry on 6.263); Aristophanes read εἰσίσθμη, as from ἰσθμός (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.264); only here in Homer
accusative of the way along which, like ἀγρούς (259), or governed by the sense of εἰρύαται (Merry on 6.264)
epithet of ships: 'curved at both ends' (or 'rowed on both sides')

265.n: Ionic 3 pl. -αται (= εἴρυνται): 'lie drawn up', as Iliad 4.248, 14.75; the scholia also offer 'guard (the road)', which Merry rejects as un-Homeric (Merry on 6.264)
πᾶσιν … ἑκάστῳ 'to all, to each': dative of possession with ἐστιν
gives the reason why the ships are drawn up along the road (Merry on 6.265)

meaning disputed: a slip or shed for each ship; Eustathius explains it as νεώριον 'dock'; Merry, rejecting a derivation from ἑστία 'hearth', connects it with ἐπιστῆναι, 'a halting place', and pictures open slips on which the ships were hauled up (Merry on 6.265); only here in Homer; second accent from enclitic ἐστιν

266.n: epic τε of a lasting fact; accent from enclitic σφʼ
Ionic ἀγορή = ἀγορά; here the place, with seats of stone (8.5–6; Merry on 6.267)
'the precinct of Poseidon', the neuter of Ποσιδήϊος (Iliad 2.506) used as a noun
epic ἀμφίς = ἀμφί, after its noun: the assembly place lies on both sides of the precinct (Merry on 6.266)

267.n: 'dragged, hauled' (ἐρύω 'draw'): blocks too big to carry (scholia, in Merry on 6.267); again 14.10; epic dat. pl. -οισι(ν)
epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative with ἀραρυῖα
= κατωρυχέεσσι, epic dat. pl. -εσσι: 'sunk in the ground' (κατορύσσω 'bury'), partly buried and partly showing (scholia, in Merry on 6.267); again 9.185

267.p: verb · pf. part. act. nom. sg. fem.
267.n: intransitive perfect ἄρηρα 'be fitted', + dat.; with ἀγορή (266): not a pavement, Merry thinks, but a low wall of blocks round it, perhaps with seats (Merry on 6.267)

269.n: 'ropes, cables', in apposition to ὅπλα (268); in Homer only in the Odyssey
'cloth', here 'sails' (σπεῖρον of a sail, 5.318); Eustathius gives a variant σπείρας 'warping cables' (Merry's critical note on 6.269)

'sharpen, taper' (ἀπό + ὀξύνω), as ἀποξῦναι 9.326, of the stake: they shave the oars to shape; Merry compares the epithet προήκεα of oars, 12.205 (Merry on 6.269); another reading, known to Eustathius and printed by Bekker, has no manuscript support (Merry's critical note on 6.269)

270.n: epic dat. pl. -εσσι; dative with μέλει
'is a care to', + dat.; personal, with βιός and φαρέτρη as subjects

272.n: epic dat. pl. -ῃσι(ν) (= αἷς): the ships

272.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. pl. masc.
272.n: 'glorying in', + dat.; Merry hears in it the Phaeacians' near friendship with their ships, which 'know the thoughts of men' (8.559) (Merry on 6.272)

273.n: epic -σσ-: 'hereafter', of time, not 'behind my back' (Merry on 6.273, citing 2.179)

274.n: 'blame, find fault' (cf. μῶμος 'blame', 2.86); subjunctive after μή (273); only here in Homer

275.n: accent from enclitic νυ; 275–288 were athetized as unsuited to the speaker (scholia, in Merry's critical note on 6.275)
epic subjunctive -ῃσι (= εἴπῃ): 'some one may say'

275.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.
275.n: 'meeting', i.e. if he met us together (Merry on 6.275)

276.n: the imagined speech of the baser man, 276–284
καλός τε μέγας τε as Iliad 21.108

277.n: emphatic at the head of the verse, followed at once by the question (Merry on 6.277)

278.n: ἦ … που 'surely … I suppose'; the alternative follows with ἤ (280)

278.p: verb · aor. part. pass. acc. sg. masc.
278.n: aorist passive of πλάζω 'drive astray': 'one driven from his course'
unaugmented, epic -σσ- (= ἐκομίσατο): both 'rescued' and 'took care of', as Iliad 1.594 (Merry on 6.278)

279.n: partitive, with τινά (278): 'one of men from far away'
explains τηλεδαπῶν: he must come from far off, since the Phaeacians have no near neighbors (Merry on 6.279)
with τινες: 'none'; accent from enclitic τινες

280.n: indefinite, accented before enclitic οἱ; the manuscripts give no variant, but τις would hardly stay short before οἱ (once ϝοι): Bekker reads ἠέ τις (Merry's critical note on 6.280)

280.p: verb · aor. part. mid. dat. sg. fem.
280.n: agrees with οἱ: 'to her, having prayed'
'much prayed for' (πολύς + ἀράομαι 'pray'); in Homer only here and 19.404

281.p: verb · aor. part. act. nom. sg. masc.

281.n: 'have to wife'; the subject is still θεός (280): 'he will have her to wife for evermore', as ἔχεις Ἑλένην 4.569 (Merry on 6.281)
epic enclitic acc., any gender: Nausicaa
ἤματα πάντα 'for ever', perhaps ironic, given the gods' inconstancy to their mortal loves (Merry on 6.281)

282.n: epic comparative (= βέλτιον): 'it is better so', bitterly sarcastic: no man of Phaeacia was good enough for her (Merry on 6.282)
crasis of καὶ αὐτή: 'she herself too'; Merry defends the crasis against other readings (Merry's critical note on 6.282)

282.p: verb · pres. part. mid. nom. sg. fem.
282.n: 'going about, going after': she went husband-hunting (Merry on 6.282)

283.n: ἄλλος + -θεν 'from': 'from some other place than this'
deictic: the Phaeacians here, Φαίηκας (284) in apposition

284.n: epic τοί = οἵ; article used as relative; accented before enclitic μιν

285.n: uncontracted future (Attic ἐροῦσιν); ὣς ἐρέουσιν as Iliad 22.108
uncontracted (Attic ὀνείδη); predicate: 'these things would be reproaches'
potential optative with κε; singular verb with neuter plural subject

286.n: dative with νεμεσῶ, not the adverb ἄλλῃ 'elsewhere'; the line after Iliad 23.494 καὶ δʼ ἄλλῳ νεμεσᾶτον, ὅτις τοιαῦτά γε ῥέζοι (Merry on 6.286)
contracted from νεμεσάω: 'feel indignation at', + dat.
optative of a purely hypothetical case; the subjunctive μίσγηται (288) narrows it to a particular instance (Merry on 6.286)

287.n: a second relative clause; a scholion says Aristarchus read it unaspirated, which Merry takes as ἠδʼ 'and' (Merry's critical note on 6.287)
= τε; epic τε after a relative
used as a noun; a scholion marks a slight pause after φίλων, and Merry takes πατρὸς καὶ μητρός as defining it (Merry on 6.287)

287.p: verb · pres. part. act. gen. pl. masc.
287.n: epic ἐών = ὤν; emphatic, 'still living' (Merry on 6.287): with Merry, all three genitives describe φίλων, the parents being the friends

288.n: 'keep company with', + dat.; subjunctive, a particular case after the optative ῥέζοι (286) (Merry on 6.286)
'open, public': a marriage openly made (cf. the adverb ἀμφαδίην, Iliad 7.196); the adjective only here in Homer
accusative of the goal with ἐλθεῖν

289.n: = δέ: δέ after a vocative, as Ἀτρεΐδη, σὺ δὲ παῦε Iliad 1.282 (Merry on 6.289)
= ὦκα, Aristarchus' reading (scholia), perhaps after ξύνες ὦκα Iliad 2.26; Merry prints ὧδʼ (Merry's critical note on 6.289); with ὦκα, evening draws on and time presses (Merry on 6.289)
epic gen. -θεν (= ἐμοῦ); genitive with ξυνίει, or with ἔπος

290.n: 'gain, obtain', + gen.; subjunctive of purpose with ὄφρα (289)

291.n: a sacred grove; ἄλσος Ἀθήνης … αἰγείρων 'a grove of Athena, of poplars' (Merry on 6.291)

292.n: material genitive with ἄλσος (291), as αἰγείρων … ἄλσος 17.208 (Merry on 6.291)

postpositive ὡς 'like', accented after its noun

epic γούνασι (= γόνασι): the suppliant's clasp of the knees

316.n: 'shining': the polished, or colored, leather or handle of the whip (Merry on 6.316)

2nd aorist ἱκόμην, + acc. of the place reached

Ionic κούρη = κόρη; Διὸς κούρῃ μεγάλοιο as 151

325.n: 'now at least'; accent from enclitic μευ
epic μευ = μου; genitive with ἄκουσον

imperfect, with ρρ after the augment: 'shatter, wreck'

unaugmented, from epic αἴδομαι (= αἰδέομαι): 'stand in awe of, respect', + acc.

unaugmented (= ἐμενέαινεν); 'rage against', + dat.; 330–331 after 1.20–21 (ἀσπερχὲς μενέαινεν)
